avoid.say: Aberdeen have never won anything big

avoid.why: Gothenburg is the club's proudest moment and fans will correct you fast.

memory: Lisbon 1967: the Lisbon Lions beat Inter 2-1 and became the first British club to win the European Cup

lingo.means: The team's nickname. The odd spelling goes back over a century and fans keep it.
Another name for the team, from the green-and-white hooped shirts.
Fans' name for Celtic Park.
The 1967 European Cup winners. Mentioning them shows you know the history.

lines.m: Going to a home game at Celtic Park.

lines.m: Fans rate the noise on big Champions League nights as the best in Britain.

lines.t: C'mon the Hoops!
lines.m: A simple rallying cry before or during a game.

lines.t: Larsson was the King of Kings.
lines.m: Fans' name for Henrik Larsson. Safe praise for a club hero.

avoid.why: The club is said with a soft S. A hard K marks you as an outsider straight away.
Fans just say Celtic. The longer name sounds like a foreign newspaper.

memory: 1961-62: Dundee won the Scottish title, then reached the European Cup semi-finals the next season

lingo.means: The short name fans use for the club.
Nickname from the navy shirts. It also sets them apart from tangerine United.
Short for Dens Park, home since 1899.

lines.m: The two Dundee grounds are about 100 yards apart on the same street, the closest in Britain.

lines.t: C'mon the Dee!
lines.m: The standard rallying cry.

lines.m: Dundee won the league in 1962, United in 1983. A gentle dig at the neighbours.

lines.t: Derby day, the whole city stops.
lines.m: The Dundee derby splits families and workplaces.

avoid.say: Dundee and Dundee United are the same club
avoid.instead: Dundee are the Dark Blues; United are the other lot
avoid.why: They are two separate clubs, and mixing them up annoys both.
Tannadice is United's ground across the street.

memory: 1982-83: United won the Scottish title for the only time, then reached the European Cup semi-finals

lingo.means: What United fans call themselves, with pride.
The team's nickname.
From the tangerine home shirts.
The home ground, about 100 yards from Dundee's Dens Park.

lines.t: We've never lost to Barcelona.
lines.m: United knocked Barcelona out of Europe in 1966 and again in 1987. Fans love telling people.

lines.t: C'mon United!
lines.m: The standard rallying cry.

lines.t: That 1987 run to the UEFA Cup final was something special.
lines.m: United reached a European final against IFK Gothenburg. Fans still talk about it.

lines.t: The New Firm was the real power in Scotland in the eighties.
lines.m: United and Aberdeen both won the league in the early 1980s.

avoid.why: Dundee is the other club in the city. Neither set of fans likes being mixed up.
Fans call the colour tangerine, and it's a point of pride.

memory: 2025: back-to-back titles took Falkirk back to the top flight for the first time in 15 years

lingo.means: Scots for 'children'. The old name for people from Falkirk, and the team's nickname.
How many locals say the town's name, without the L.
The old ground, used until 2003. Older fans still talk about it fondly.

lines.t: Better meddle wi' the deil than the Bairns o' Fa'kirk.
lines.m: The old town motto: you'd be safer messing with the devil than with Falkirk folk.

lines.t: C'mon the Bairns!
lines.m: The usual rallying cry.

lines.t: Fifteen years out of the top flight felt like forever.
lines.m: Fans remember the long wait before the 2025 promotion.

lines.t: Nothing beats beating the Pars.
lines.m: Wins over Dunfermline, just across the Forth, are the ones fans enjoy most.

avoid.why: The club left Brockville in 2003, so calling it home is out of date.
It's the Scots word for children, not a farm building.

memory: 2012: Hearts beat Hibs 5-1 in the Scottish Cup final at Hampden

lingo.means: Hearts fans, and the team. It grew out of 'Jam Tarts'.
Rhyming slang for Hearts. Used with affection.
The area of west Edinburgh around Tynecastle. 'Going down Gorgie' means going to the game.

lines.m: Just saying the score of the 2012 cup final is enough to wind up a Hibs fan.

lines.t: Going down Gorgie on Saturday?
lines.m: Asking a mate if they're going to Tynecastle.

lines.t: Tynecastle is the loudest ground in Scotland for its size.
lines.m: Fans boast that the steep, tight stands make it a tough place for visitors.

lines.t: C'mon the Hearts!
lines.m: Rallying cry. Older fans often say 'the Hearts'.

avoid.why: Nobody uses the full name in conversation, and the club is always plural.
The name is historical. The club plays in Gorgie, Edinburgh.
The Edinburgh derby is a real rivalry. Hearts fans never warm to Hibs.

memory: 2016: Hibs beat Rangers 3-2 to win the Scottish Cup for the first time since 1902

lingo.means: What everyone calls the club. The full name, Hibernian, is rarely used.
The team's nickname. It rhymes with 'high', not 'hip'.
Short for 'cabbage and ribs', rhyming slang for Hibs.
The great forward line of the late 1940s and 1950s: Smith, Johnstone, Reilly, Turnbull and Ormond.

lines.t: 114 years we waited, and it was worth every one.
lines.m: The 2016 Scottish Cup win ended a wait going back to 1902.

lines.m: Fans sing the Proclaimers' 'Sunshine on Leith'. After the 2016 final it became legendary.

lines.t: Easter Road on derby day, nothing like it.
lines.m: Home games against Hearts are the biggest of the season.

lines.m: Hibs fans' joking way of brushing off the 5-1 cup final defeat to Hearts.

avoid.why: Hibees starts like 'high'. Saying it like 'hip' is a giveaway.
The full name sounds formal. Everyone just says Hibs.

memory: 1965: Killie won their only league title on the last day, beating Hearts 2-0 at Tynecastle

lingo.means: The club's universal nickname, and the local name for the town.

lines.m: The pie is part of the matchday ritual at Rugby Park.

lines.t: We won the league at Tynecastle in '65.
lines.m: The 1965 title, won on the final day. Killie's proudest moment.

lines.t: C'mon Killie!
lines.m: The standard rallying cry.

lines.m: The Ayrshire derby is the local game that matters most.

avoid.say: Kilmarnock are the oldest club in Scotland
avoid.instead: Killie are the oldest club in the Premiership
avoid.why: Queen's Park are older. Fans claim the top-flight record instead.

memory: 1991: Motherwell beat Dundee United 4-3 after extra time in a classic Scottish Cup final

Nickname from the town's steelworks history.
The club colours, worn since 1913.

lines.t: C'mon the Well!
lines.m: The classic Motherwell rallying cry.

lines.t: The '91 final was the best Scottish Cup final ever.
lines.m: Motherwell's 4-3 win over Dundee United is a fan favourite.

lines.m: Motherwell's only league title. Fans bring it up with a grin.

lines.t: Beat Hamilton and it's a good week.
lines.m: The Lanarkshire derby is the local game fans care about most.

avoid.why: Fans are particular about the club colours.
The town is in Lanarkshire, south-east of Glasgow, and locals are proud of it.

memory: 1972: Rangers beat Dynamo Moscow 3-2 at the Camp Nou to win the European Cup Winners' Cup

Rhyming slang for 'Gers'. That's why fans call themselves the Bears.

A traditional nickname for the team.

lines.m: The 1972 Cup Winners' Cup win at the Camp Nou.

lines.m: Tina Turner's 'Simply the Best' is the Ibrox victory song.

lines.t: C'mon the Gers!
lines.m: The standard rallying cry.

lines.m: Fans love the big European games. Rangers reached UEFA finals in 2008 and 2022.

lines.m: Rangers lost the Europa League final to Eintracht Frankfurt on penalties. Sympathy goes down well.

avoid.say: the Gers with a hard G
avoid.why: It's short for Rangers, so the G stays soft.
The first syllable rhymes with 'eye'.

avoid.say: Celtic Park is the best ground in Glasgow
avoid.why: Never praise the rival ground to a Rangers fan.

memory: 2020-21: Saints won both the League Cup and the Scottish Cup in the same season

Perth's old name, which gave the club its name.
Short for McDiarmid Park, home since 1989.

lines.m: The standard rallying cry.

lines.m: The 2014 Scottish Cup, the first big trophy in the club's history.

lines.m: The Tayside derbies are the games fans care about most.

avoid.why: The name comes from Perth's old name. Johnstone is a different town, near Paisley.
Both are called Saints, but St Mirren are from Paisley. Mixing them up is a classic slip.

memory: 1987: St Mirren beat Dundee United 1-0 after extra time to win the Scottish Cup

lingo.means: People from Paisley are known as Buddies, and so are the team and their fans.
The other nickname, from Saint Mirin, Paisley's patron saint.

lines.m: Fans are proud of the team's habit of winning big European games late.

lines.m: Beating Real Madrid matters more than almost anything.

'The big snake', the club symbol, taken from Milan's coat of arms.

lines.m: 'Come on Inter!'

lines.m: Inter have played every Serie A season. Fans enjoy reminding Milan and Juve.

lines.t: Forza Juve!

lines.m: Juve fans expect trophies every season.

lines.t: Nine in a row. Say no more.
lines.m: The run of league titles from 2012 to 2020.

avoid.why: The J is said like a Y in Italian.

memory: 1987: Napoli's first Scudetto (league title), led by Diego Maradona

lingo.means: From Parthenope, the ancient name of Naples. English commentators use it a lot.
'The Blues', from the sky-blue shirts.
Neapolitan for 'the donkey', the club's mascot.

lines.m: 'Come on Napoli, always!' A common sign-off among fans.

Roman slang for 'Come on!'. You'll hear 'Daje Roma' everywhere.

lines.t: The derby is the only game that matters in this city.
lines.m: Roma against Lazio splits Rome down the middle.

Lazio share the city and the stadium. Say this and you'll start an argument.

memory: 2000: Lazio won the Scudetto in the club's centenary season

Lazio fans.
'The Eagles', from the eagle on the crest.

lines.t: Forza Lazio!

'The Reds', from the red shirts.

'The black-and-yellows', from the club colours.
